Adverse Effects and Treatment Adverse effects are common and may be severe during the treatment of African trypanosomiasis with melar- soprol. It may be difficult to distinguish between ef- fects of the disease, Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions re- sulting from the release of antigens from trypanosomes killed by melarsoprol, and adverse effects due to the drug’s arsenic content or to hypersensitivity. For the adverse effects of arsenic and their treatment, see Ar- senic Trioxide, p.2260.
